key_insight: An instantaneous generalized total-enthalpy similarity closes both mean and fluctuating velocity–temperature relations in compressible turbulent boundary layers, unifying Reynolds-analogy-style behavior from averages to fluctuations.
engineering_relevance: This provides a parameter-free, physics-based way to predict wall-heat-transfer–velocity coupling across Mach number and thermal boundary conditions, useful for high-speed aerothermal design and turbulence modeling.
method: Use the instantaneous relation that generalized total enthalpy minus wall value is proportional to local velocity.
Recover the mean generalized Reynolds analogy from the same closure.
Derive the fluctuating-field ratio using universal streamwise energy fraction, production–dissipation quasi-equilibrium, and Obukhov–Corrsin cutoff universality.
evidence_signal: Validated against compressible boundary-layer DNS data across Mach numbers and wall thermal conditions, with the predicted fluctuating relation collapsing to unity and reproducing the refined strong Reynolds analogy benchmark.
watch_item: The closure relies on assumed universality constants and equilibrium/cutoff-scale arguments, so robustness may weaken in strongly nonequilibrium flows or outside the DNS-covered regime.
paper_title: Generalized Reynolds Analogy for Compressible Turbulent Boundary Layers: Unified Velocity-Temperature Relations from Mean to Fluctuating Field
